rationale_evidence.statement: Audits four hash/fold/structural-identity constructions against what each does and does not establish: exact equivalence (25J.2, canonical serialization plus hash) establishes artifact identity only relative to a fixed serialization, not semantic equality or observation identity; id=H(P,e,c,t,Pi) establishes a key, not a definition (inconsistent under mutable state, executed); a raw byte hash (25I.5) is explicitly rejected by the corpus as sufficient (25I.29: identity cannot simply be Hash(currentRepresentation)); fold equality (25I.31, 258.11) is decidable but explicitly insufficient as behavioural equivalence. Concludes H(x)=H(y) requires a specified serialization, canonicalization, collision model, and scope, of which three of the four are unspecified in the corpus.

rationale_evidence.anchor: ## §18 The thirteen required negative results ... $$\boxed{\textbf{13 of 13 falsified. Four by execution, nine from the corpus. Zero survived.}}$$
rationale_evidence.statement: Presents the full thirteen-item required-negative-results table (mandate section 18): (1) one universal equality relation exists -- falsified by 261.19's boxed no-single-relation-adequate conclusion; (2) semantic equality is already fully specified -- falsified by the equiv/approx formula collision (G-67); (3) observational equivalence is defined at K level -- falsified since 𝒪_K is not closed; (4) approx_X is the corpus's approx -- falsified, three rival indexings exist (𝒪, policy, axis-subset); (5) Sigma-order implies K-order -- falsified, K carries content/provenance/history/governance/events/retraction none of which is a Sigma coordinate; (6) structural equality is a congruence -- falsified by execution (TraceOrigin toy model); (7) a hash identity is semantic identity -- falsified by execution (key-order and locale ambiguity); (8) finite-sample agreement proves equality -- falsified by execution (f,g example); (9) provenance relevance is an executable predicate -- falsified, only a principle exists; (10) Decision 3 alone closes equality -- falsified, 𝒪_K and 𝒯 both still open and the equiv/approx conflict remains; (11) the 32 projections close observational equivalence -- falsified, they are Sigma-level and the K-to-Sigma projection itself is unspecified; (12) Step 288 can close kernel selection independently of Step 261 -- falsified, 0 of 6 conditions resolved; (13) equality closure automatically yields an implementable kernel -- falsified, the quotient is not implementable and delta's commit case is unspecifiable. Overall: 13 of 13 falsified, four by direct execution and nine from corpus citation, zero surviving.
